title: Lead-Time-Conditioned Convex Stacked Ensemble for Medium-Term Electricity Load Forecasting (IET GTD, full text)
note: Fetched in full (open access); first-published date from the research call's source entry for this page. Proposes LTCC: per-horizon convex weights fitted on out-of-fold forecasts, then re-normalised online from past losses (AdaHedge, no learning rate). Abstract: competitive with the strongest comparator but not uniformly better; none of the 12 differences is significant.

title: Same article: data and design
note: Target: ENTSO-E actual total load for ES, FR, GR, PT, hourly, resampled to daily mean. Each origin uses the previous 28 days and forecasts 7 daily values; origins move by one week through 2025 (53 origins, 365 scored dates). Nine base learners: SARIMA, XGBoost, LightGBM, LSTM, GRU, CNN-LSTM, TCN, DLinear, Transformer; fitted on 2015 to 2024, not retrained during 2025.

title: Same article: covariates and leakage controls
note: Temperature, precipitation, wind, heating and cooling degree days enter only as 28 days of history. No weather is given for the 7 forecast days; only calendar and holiday fields are known-future. The paper says future weather, if added, would have to be archived forecasts. Eleven leakage controls are listed as passed, three of them by perturbation tests.

title: Same article: main results table
note: 2025 MAE in MW, LTCC vs seasonal naive: ES 785.12 vs 1281.74, FR 2214.15 vs 3329.48, GR 260.71 vs 413.16, PT 195.54 vs 283.22. LTCC SMAPE: ES 2.891, FR 4.177, GR 4.430, PT 3.277 percent. LTCC is first in 3 of 12 country-metric cells, second in 4, and beats every base learner in 9 of 12. Mean gain over the nine base learners: MAE 12.68, RMSE 11.87, SMAPE 12.92 percent.

title: Same article: against the strongest comparator, significance
note: Against the best non-LTCC method per cell LTCC differs by -2.24 to +1.37 percent (FR RMSE: GRU 3155.40 vs 3226.21; PT MAE: unconstrained stack 197.14 vs 195.54). Paired tests on 365 daily losses: nothing significant; all twelve 95 percent intervals include zero. Mean rank 2.67 of 18 methods, worst rank 5. The frozen online setting is not the best of a 324-point grid in any market.

title: Same article: availability and compute
note: Data availability statement: load data public on ENTSO-E; processed data and code only from the corresponding author on request. No repository or data record is linked. Runs used a supercomputer node with one GPU and 72 cores; about 29 minutes of cross-validation training per country plus about 6 minutes final fit. No foundation model is tested. Funded by Horizon Europe (TWINVEST).

title: Research source 1: the journal article
note: Research call (standard, LinkedIn excluded). Its only supporting source is the article itself: week-ahead at daily resolution, nine base learners, weather as history only, code on request. The source entry adds that the authors say the online layer's design was partly motivated by behaviour seen in the 2025 evaluation year and has not been tested on later years or other markets.

title: Research source 2: author profile page listing an earlier record of the same title
note: Profile of the senior author. Lists a record with the same title and authors, DOI 10.22541/au.177431975.56166018/v1, dated 24 March 2026, whose summary describes a simpler version (weights through a softmax, ensemble always better than the standalone models, about 10 percent lower error). Secondary listing; the record itself was not read.
